statement: When a degraded input can move an aggregate in either direction, no per-component treatment makes the aggregate safe: abstain on the aggregate and keep the components visible. v27 left A2's shallow-clone abstention out of the composite and then capped the verdict; dropping a criterion from a mean moves the mean toward the others, so on 77 synthetic shallow checkouts 52 composites fell below their full clone and 11 rose above it, and the cap only bounded the rises. Under the operator's ruling the report abstains instead, with an instruction to fetch the history, and every criterion's reading stays byte-identical. Rule: before excluding, zeroing or capping, ask whether the degraded input can push the aggregate both ways; if so, withhold the aggregate, not the component.
